'''''Halimione portulacoides''''', commonly known as '''sea purslane''',<ref>{{cite book |author1=David Chapman |title=Exploring the Cornish Coast |date=2008 |publisher=Alison Hodge |location=[[Penzance]] |isbn=9780906720561 |page=78}}</ref> is a [[shrub]] found in [[Eurasia]].

== Description ==
The [[perennial]] plant grows to {{Convert|1|m|ft|abbr=off|frac=2}} in height.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Francis-Baker |first=Tiffany |title=Concise Foraging Guide |date=2021 |publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing|Bloomsbury]] |isbn=978-1-4729-8474-6 |series=[[The Wildlife Trusts]] |location=London |pages=55}}</ref> The leaves are thick and oval-shaped, with a powdery surface.<ref name=":0" /> In northern temperate climates it flowers from July to September. The flowers are small, borne in short clusters,<ref name=":0" /> [[monoecious]], and [[Anemophily|pollinated by wind]].

== Taxonomy ==
[[Botanical synonym]]s include ''Atriplex portulacoides'' L. and ''Obione portulacoides'' (L.) Moq. Recent phylogenetic research revealed that ''Halimione'' is a distinct genus and cannot be included in ''[[Atriplex]]''.<ref name="pmid21616801">{{cite journal |vauthors=Kadereit G, Mavrodiev EV, Zacharias EH, Sukhorukov AP |date=October 2010 |title=Molecular phylogeny of Atripliceae (Chenopodioideae, Chenopodiaceae): Implications for systematics, biogeography, flower and fruit evolution, and the origin of C4 photosynthesis |journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=97 |issue=10 |pages=1664–87 |doi=10.3732/ajb.1000169 |pmid=21616801}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Halimione portulacoides'' occurs at the sea shores of [[Western Europe|western]] and [[southern Europe]], and from the [[Mediterranean Sea]] to [[western Asia]].<ref>{{cite web | vauthors = Uotila P, ((''Halimione portulacoides'' (L.) Aellen)) | title = Chenopodiaceae (pro parte majore). | work = Euro+Med Plantbase - the information resource for Euro-Mediterranean plant diversity. | date = 2011 | url = http://ww2.bgbm.org/euroPlusMed/PTaxonDetail.asp?UUID=B289DD77-EEFE-4C56-A404-0265D9519DFD | access-date = 2012-12-14 }}</ref> A [[halophyte]], it is found in [[salt marsh]]es and coastal [[dune]]s, and is usually flooded at high [[tide]].

== Uses ==
The [[edible leaves]] can be eaten raw in [[salad]]s or cooked as a [[potherb]].<ref name=":0" /> They are thick and succulent with a crunchy texture and a natural saltiness.<ref>{{cite web |title=Halimione portulacoides Sea Purslane PFAF Plant Database |url=http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Halimione+portulacoides |work=pfaf.org}}</ref> The leaves are good for human and animal health as they contain important [[micronutrient]]s like zinc, iron, copper, and cobalt.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Zanella L, Vianello F |date=October 2020 |title=Functional Food from Endangered Ecosystems: ''Atriplex portulacoides'' as a Case Study |journal=Foods |volume=9 |issue=11 |pages=1533 |doi=10.3390/foods9111533 |pmc=7692200 |pmid=33114436 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
